ut_the_box_canyon_ice_climbs.blurb: A side canyon off Maple Canyon in central Utah that fills with winter ice. All 18 climbs here are water ice, running from easy WI2 and WI3 steps up through a solid middle block of WI4 and WI5 to a few WI6 lines, so it suits climbers with some experience more than first-timers. Walls rise several hundred feet, and the harder routes are bigger and more serious than the ones along the main canyon road. Whether anything is in condition depends on snowfall and a melt and refreeze cycle, and it can change fast. Plan on two ropes for the rappels.
ut_the_box_canyon_ice_climbs.approach: Walk up the canyon road from the entrance, a little under a mile, to the side canyon on the right. The road is often snow covered in ice season, so expect to hike or ski.

ut_fern_s_ledge.blurb: A short, slightly overhanging limestone cliff in South Willow Canyon, in the Stansbury Mountains west of Salt Lake City. Its 18 routes are all bolted sport lines, and nearly all of them are hard: a dozen or so sit in the low and mid 5.12s, with several 5.13s and a couple of 5.11s plus one easier 5.9 line. Expect bouldery moves on sharp, textured rock. It faces east, so it takes morning sun, and it is a poor choice for anyone still working below 5.11.

ut_question_mark_wall.blurb: A big alpine wall in the Lone Peak Cirque of the central Wasatch, sitting near 11,000 feet. Most of its 18 climbs are multi-pitch trad or alpine lines, and the grades cover a wide range: a handful in the 5.8 range, a few at 5.10, then a hard group from 5.11 into the low 5.13s and beyond. Everything starts from a ledge reached by a wandering 5.4 scramble, and the way off is east along the top and down a ramp. Getting into the cirque at all is a long, strenuous day or several, so this is a commitment for fit, experienced parties.

ut_south_narrows.blurb: The creek-side face of the main crag in the Upper Narrows, a limestone gorge in South Willow Canyon in the Stansbury Mountains. All 18 routes are bolted sport climbs, ranging from a few 5.10s through a thick middle of 5.11 and 5.12 to several 5.13s and one 5.14. The Narrows is shaded in summer, which makes it a good warm-season option, but it is busiest on weekends, so a weekday visit is quieter. The lower bolts on some south-side lines may call for a stick clip.

ut_north_and_west_faces.blurb: Two faces of Challenge Buttress in Big Cottonwood Canyon, close to the road and a quick walk in. The 18 routes mix older trad lines with newer bolted sport climbs, with a few top-rope options, and they run from 5.7 or 5.8 through a good block of 5.9 to 5.11. The quartzite can look dirty but cleans up with traffic. Many of the trad routes are old and rely on natural gear, so some skill placing protection helps. It is popular for after-work sessions and can be crowded.
ut_north_and_west_faces.parking_note: Leave the car at the Stairs Gulch pullout, the same place used for the other climbing in that gulch, and start up the trail from there.

ut_rubicon_the.blurb: A wall of short bolted basalt routes in Crawdad Canyon near Veyo, north of St. George in southwest Utah. All 18 climbs are sport routes, with one 5.8, a couple of 5.10s, and a big cluster of 5.11 followed by a handful of 5.12s, so it suits climbers who are comfortable in the 5.11 range. The wall stays shaded for most of the day, which makes it one of the better choices for beating the heat in a southern Utah summer. The routes sit just across the stream from the parking and pool area.

ut_cathedral_the.blurb: A short cliff in Ferguson Canyon, a small canyon between Big Cottonwood and Little Cottonwood in the central Wasatch, sitting just up-canyon from the Watchtower. It carries 18 routes, mostly traditional with a few sport lines, on quartz monzonite, and it has a steep south face, an easy west face and a varied north face. Grades run from 5.7 through a solid block of 5.10 and 5.11 up to a few 5.12s. The canyon is wooded and mostly shaded, which suits summer days. Some fixed gear can be suspect, so bring your own.
